The All-Share Index (ASI) declined by 989.00 points, representing a loss of 0.40 per cent to close at 248,329.65 points. Also, market capitalisation lost N642 billion to close at N 161.238 trillion.
The downturn was driven by price depreciation in large and medium capitalised stocks amongst which are; Aradel Holdings, Zenith Bank, eTranzact International, Meyer and Champion Breweries.
Despite the bearish close, market sentiment remained marginally positive, with 26 advancers, outweighing 25 decliners. Critical Minerals Financing Corporation (CMFC) and McNichols emerged the highest price gainer of 10 per cent each to close at N3.52 and N4.95 respectively, while Chellaram followed with a gain of 9.79 per cent to close at N10.65, per share.
Living Trust Mortgage Bank rose by 9.77 per cent to close at N2.81, while Veritas Kapital Assurance appreciated by 9.71 per cent to close at N1.13, per share.
On the other side, Aradel Holdings led others on the losers’ chart with 10 per cent to close at N1,166.40, per share. eTranzact International followed with a decline of 9.86 per cent to close at N15.55, while Transnational Express shed 9.26 per cent to close at N2.45, per share.
Meyer went down by 8.86 per cent to close at N15.95, while Champion Breweries depreciated by 8.85 per cent to close at N11.85, per share.
Trading activity was mixed, as turnover and deal count increased by 16.87 per cent and 4.93 per cent to N26.61 billion and 32,572 transactions, respectively, while volume declined by 20.02 per cent to 451.14 million shares.
Looking ahead, Cowry Assets Management Limited said, “sustained profit-taking in heavyweight counters and sectoral weakness could constrain near-term recovery, although selective bargain-hunting and marginally positive market breadth may provide some support.”
